data.title: Enqueue
data.tagline: Enqueue puts work into a queue so a request can receive a task ID before a later processor runs it
data.learningOutcome: You can distinguish queue acceptance from task completion and avoid assuming an order or exactly-once processing.
data.description: After someone uploads a video, the API can enqueue a transcoding task and return a task ID while the page shows queued, processing, or completed. Batch notifications can use the same pattern. A successful enqueue means the queue accepted the task, not that transcoding or delivery has finished; queues also do not automatically promise FIFO ordering or exactly-once processing.

learning.assumes: You have seen a page show queued work or completion later.
learning.outcome: You can distinguish queue acceptance from task completion and avoid assuming an order or exactly-once processing.

explanation.title: Avoid blocking the request
explanation.text: If the upload request performs transcoding directly, the user waits and a processing failure can look like an upload failure. Enqueueing accepts the task and returns its ID first.

explanation.title: Bring status back
explanation.text: A later processor updates queued, processing, completed, or failed state. The page looks up those results with the task ID; failures can be retried or reported under the system rules.

explanation.title: Improvement is observable
explanation.text: The upload request finishes sooner, status changes are visible, and failures are tied to a task. Enqueueing still does not promise FIFO order or exactly-once processing.

data.boundary: Enqueueing is not a completion notification, permanent storage, or a strict ordering promise. Check the queue's ordering, capacity, and failure rules before making those assumptions.

lessonPractice.title: The upload API returned a task ID, but transcoding is not finished. What should the page show?

options.label: Show queued or processing, and use the task ID to check later status
options.feedback: Correct. The task ID makes the work trackable, but enqueueing does not mean transcoding has finished.

options.label: Show completed because the task was successfully written to the queue
options.feedback: Writing to the queue only means the task was accepted. You still need to check when processing starts and whether it succeeds.

options.label: Keep the upload request open until transcoding finishes, then return the task ID
options.feedback: That puts the long operation back inside the upload request, making timeouts more likely.

data.agentPrompt: Enqueue the transcoding task after upload and return a trackable task ID immediately. Show queued, processing, completed, and failed states. Verify that the task enters the queue, failures reach status lookup, and enqueue success is not shown as transcoding completion.
